title: AI News Radar
description: Real-time panoramic intelligence radar for global frontier AI breakthroughs.

items.title: Linq, which offers texting and calling infrastructure for AI agents, raised a $90M Series B led by a16z, following a $20M Series A in February (Harper Harwell/Birmingham Business Journal)
items.content_text: Linq, a provider of specialized communication infrastructure for AI agents, has secured $90 million in Series B funding led by Andreessen Horowitz (a16z). This financing follows a $20 million Series A round in February, underscoring rapid capital deployment into the foundational connectivity layer of the AI agent ecosystem.

items.title: Bloomberg analysis of 10 million job postings shows AI-exposed roles in China fell 10 percentage points faster than others
items.content_text: of nearly 10 million job postings reveals that AI is significantly disrupting China's labor market, disproportionately affecting entry-level and creative roles. Vulnerable positions have seen a demand decline 10 percentage points sharper than non-impacted roles, with research from ShanghaiTech University and the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences confirming structural shifts including role consolidation and quiet staff reductions at major internet firms.

items.title: Anthropic mathematician Levent Alpöge says he used Claude to prove the 167-year-old Riemann hypothesis and posts the proof in the Lean programming language (Joseph Howlett/Scientific American)
items.content_text: Levent Alpöge, a mathematician and employee at artificial intelligence company Anthropic, claimed on Friday to have proven the most famous problem in all of mathematics using an LLM. “I believe I have, working with Claude, discovered a proof of the Riemann Hypothesis,” Alpöge wrote in a statement posted on his website. items.title: Anthropic Share Slump Nearly Erases IPO Pop As AI Trade Unravels
items.content_text: Anthropic PBC shares erased much of their first-day jump on Friday, testing investors' faith after the AI lab delivered the biggest initial public offering in history.

items.title: Apple joins the race for AI agents that control your device while raising new barriers for competitors
items.content_text: After Meta, OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google launched their own AI agents, Apple is now building one too - while making it harder for rivals to access its devices. According to a job listing, Apple is hiring a senior engineer to lead the project as a rival to Muse, Dots, Duet, and Grok Bots. Privacy is expected to be central to the new agent, with permission models and sandboxing (protected test environments). items.title: Nvidia bets at least $500 million on Inception's diffusion models to strengthen its open-source Nemotron lineup
items.content_text: Nvidia is in advanced talks to acquire AI startup Inception for at least $500 million, including full-time integration of founders Stefano Ermon, Aditya Grover, and Volodymyr Kuleshov. Inception specializes in diffusion-based language models, such as Mercury 3, which refine responses globally rather than token-by-token. This acquisition is designed to enhance Nvidia's Nemotron open-source lineup and accelerate its physical simulation capabilities for robotics.

items.title: The week everything fell apart
items.content_text: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang is embroiled in a growing scandal involving the alleged illegal smuggling of chips to China, fueling speculation regarding his potential exit. The core controversy centers on Nvidia’s compliance failures and internal control deficiencies amid increasingly stringent US export restrictions.

items.title: Anthropic raises $93.5 billion total as underwriters scoop up ‘greenshoe’ overallotment
items.content_text: AI firm Anthropic completed its historic IPO on Nasdaq, raising a total of $93.5 billion after underwriters exercised the greenshoe option for an additional $12.2 billion. Simultaneously, the company closed a $26 billion private placement involving major tech entities like AMD, Google, Microsoft, and Nvidia, bringing total gross proceeds to $119.5 billion.

items.title: Google's latest homepage update pushes its search engine further toward an AI answer engine
items.content_text: Google is rolling out a collapsible sidebar globally on its Desktop Search homepage, making AI search even easier to access. Announced on X by Google Search VP Robby Stein, the feature lets users easily find and reopen recent AI searches. Sitting on the left side of the AI Mode interface, it lets users start new threads, search existing ones, create notebooks, and open recent queries and settings. Stein said people are increasingly asking Google Search questions that a single query can't answer

items.title: Uber tests rides for kids as young as 10, with extra pay for drivers
items.content_text: Uber has launched the 'Uber Kids' pilot program in Austin, Nashville, and Madison, lowering the minimum ride-hailing age to 10. The service mandates parental onboarding, real-time video monitoring, PIN verification, and GPS-based off-course detection, while offering participating high-rated drivers a $7 premium per trip.

items.title: Threats, Insults, Settlements: How Jensen Huang Made Humiliation Routine
items.content_text: Nvidia founder and CEO Jensen Huang has reportedly utilized aggressive management tactics, allegedly stating that as employees achieve financial independence due to the company's soaring market cap, humiliation becomes the primary tool to ensure continued high-intensity output. This governance philosophy has triggered internal concerns regarding organizational cohesion and long-term talent retention.

items.title: Threats, Insults, Settlements: How Jensen Huang Made Humiliation Routine
items.content_text: As Nvidia became wealthier and wealthier in recent years, Jensen Huang grew increasingly frustrated with his staff. He told groups of subordinates that they had become so rich that he couldn’t motivate them simply with money, according to three people who spoke on the condition of anonymity to discuss confidential conversations. items.title: Signal is blocking Gemini and Siri AI from reading your screen
items.content_text: Meredith Whittaker, President of Signal, announced that integrated OS-level AI agents undermine app-level privacy. To mitigate this, Signal has disabled screenshot functionality on iOS and Android to prevent AI assistants from harvesting encrypted message data, while demanding that OS providers implement transparent technical controls for developer-side AI access management.

items.title: Muse Is Unleashing a World of Pettiness on Instagram
items.content_text: Meta's AI assistant Muse is being widely utilized by users to execute automated, bulk unfollow operations. The tool accurately identifies non-reciprocal followers and generates detailed category lists, while mitigating the risk of account suspension typically associated with third-party automated scripts.

items.title: China tightens approvals for offshore listings by red-chip firms, threatening Hong Kong IPO market: Reuters
items.content_text: The China Securities Regulatory Commission (CSRC) has informed law firms that red-chip companies established after the 2023 administrative measures for overseas securities offerings must relocate their place of incorporation to mainland China to receive approval for offshore listings. This policy signals a rigorous shift toward enforcing substantive domestic jurisdiction over overseas fundraising vehicles.

items.title: Ex-Alibaba Star’s AI Startup Doubles Valuation to $5 Billion
items.content_text: A generative AI startup founded by the former head of Alibaba Group's AI division has secured new funding, doubling its valuation to $5 billion within a few months. This capital injection underscores sustained investor confidence in the commercial viability of high-tier foundational model developers.

items.title: Signal to Restrict Screenshots to Block AI Agents, Urges Regulation on Apple, Google and Microsoft
items.content_text: Signal has introduced default screenshot restrictions to prevent OS-level AI agents, such as Apple Siri and Google Gemini, from scraping screen data and bypassing end-to-end encryption. The company stated that these agents pose a severe privacy threat by leveraging system-level permissions and has urged Apple, Google, and Microsoft to provide more granular platform control tools.

items.title: Regular Tech Bros Are Worried About Honeypots
items.content_text: Executives and core engineers in Silicon Valley are increasingly vigilant against corporate espionage facilitated through romantic relationships. Business intelligence and high-end matchmaking firms report a surge in demand for comprehensive background checks, non-disclosure agreements, and behavioral audits as standard defensive measures against the leakage of sensitive intellectual property.

items.title: SK Hynix to Convert Kioxia Bond and Become Top Shareholder
items.content_text: SK Hynix is considering converting its holdings in Kioxia convertible bonds into equity. This move is intended to solidify SK Hynix's strategic position as the largest shareholder of the Japanese NAND flash manufacturer amidst semiconductor market volatility and a cooling AI investment cycle.

items.title: SK Hynix To Be Kioxia S Top Shareholder After Bond Conversion
items.content_text: SK Hynix has announced plans to convert its holdings of Kioxia bonds into equity, resulting in a 14.1% stake and making the South Korean memory giant the largest shareholder in the Japanese storage manufacturer. This move is designed to deepen supply chain cooperation within the memory sector and strengthen strategic leverage in the NAND flash market.

items.title: Hermes Agent's Collective Wisdom feature turns one employee's AI trick into the whole team's skill
items.content_text: AI research lab Nous Research has launched an enterprise version of Hermes Agent, integrated into Microsoft Teams and secured within Azure Container Apps sandboxes. The new 'Collective Wisdom' feature enables employees to convert successful automated workflows into team-wide shared assets, while ensuring that internal operational data is excluded from third-party model training.

items.title: AI Threatens to Make China’s Jobs Slump Much Worse
items.content_text: Gartner projects a net gain of 1.7 million jobs by 2030, with 10.6 million created against 8.9 million lost globally. Chief forecaster John Lovelock notes that firms are transitioning from 'deferred hiring' to productive deployment, expecting a rebound in labor demand as AI systems move past the Trough of Disillusionment.

items.title: Google is rolling out a collapsible sidebar on its desktop Search homepage, letting users easily find and resume recent AI searches (Barry Schwartz/Search Engine Roundtable)
items.content_text: Google has officially rolled out a collapsible sidebar on its desktop Search homepage, a strategic move by its search experience division to enhance continuity for users engaged in multi-turn AI queries. The feature is designed to shift search patterns from one-off interactions toward long-term engagement by providing a persistent hub for recent AI-generated tasks.

items.title: Singapore-Based DayOne Is Said to Pause US IPO Plans on Data Center, Market Concerns
items.content_text: Singapore-based DayOne Data Centers has shelved its planned US IPO amid cooling market valuations for AI infrastructure and intensifying regulatory scrutiny. Despite efforts to navigate the AI compute demand surge, the company faces significant headwinds from investor skepticism regarding data center asset sustainability and strict US regulations on the export of advanced AI hardware to entities with China-linked operations.

items.title: This 16-Year-Old Founded an AI Missile Startup. He’s Targeting ‘Cost per Kill’
items.content_text: At 16 years old, Henrijs Dandzbergs is too young to vote. Or drink. Or smoke. Or drive unsupervised. items.title: Samsung names Choi Won-Joon head of its mobile division, replacing TM Roh, who stays as Samsung co-CEO, and Sang Joon Hwang to lead its memory business (Ben Schoon/9to5Google)
items.content_text: Samsung Electronics has announced a leadership transition in its MX (Mobile Experience) business unit, appointing Chief Operating Officer Choi Won-Joon as the new head of the mobile division to oversee post-Galaxy S26 and Z Fold 8 product strategy. TM Roh will step down from the mobile leadership role but will retain his position as Samsung Electronics co-CEO, focusing on broader corporate strategy and cross-divisional integration.

items.title: Nscale’s ByteDance Deal Faces Scrutiny Under US Chip Curbs
items.content_text: Nscale, a UK-based AI infrastructure provider, faces intense scrutiny from US export regulators during its IPO process due to its rental agreement providing Nvidia B200 GPU access to a ByteDance subsidiary in Singapore. The contract, which once accounted for 73% of Nscale's revenue, now sits at the center of a compliance crisis exacerbated by November 2026 export controls and revelations of the client's ties to US-blacklisted entities, threatening the company's financial transparency and listing prospects.

items.title: Industrial monitoring startup BrightAI closes $97M investment
items.content_text: BrightAI Inc., a startup that helps industrial companies detect malfunctioning equipment, has raised $97 million in funding. Smith Point Capital led the Series A round. BrightAI said in its Wednesday announcement of the deal that a number of other venture capital firms contributed as well. They were joined by GE Vernova Inc., an energy equipment company that emerged from the 2024 split-up of General Electric Co. items.title: Tech stocks fall as Anthropic IPO fails to reignite AI trade
items.content_text: Technology stocks in Asia fell on Friday as Anthropic’s record listing in New York rattled the region’s equity markets and failed to reverse losses from a deepening sell-off in AI companies. Shares of SoftBank, which holds a roughly 13 per cent stake in OpenAI, sank more than 15 per cent, while Japan’s Nikkei 225 index shed nearly 5 per cent.
